text: I shoulder through the rain and the crowd to the notice board and read the fresh postings on the new taxes, the curfew, and the missing patrol, looking for names, places, and how recently the ink was put up.
motivation: The board is the plainest sign of what is wrong at this gate, and I can read it without pinning myself to one stranger's talk.
intended: I want the concrete details of the patrol warning and the new rules before I try to pass the guards.

text: I turn northwest from the board and look for the old crates and the muddy track the posting names, trying to see how far that route sits from the gate and whether anyone is already heading that way.
motivation: The missing patrol was last sent that way this morning, and the ink is still damp.
intended: I want to spot the track and the crates so I can judge whether I can look into the patrol before the dusk curfew.

text: I walk the few dozen paces to the old crates and check the muddy ruts for fresh boot prints or drag marks, then listen toward the underbrush for whatever is moving out there.
motivation: The track the missing patrol took is empty and close, and something is still moving along it.
intended: I want a clear sign of which way the patrol went and whether that sound is worth following before dusk.

text: I follow the muddy track a short way past the crates into the underbrush, keeping low and quiet, to get a look at whatever is moving out there.
motivation: The ruts told me nothing, but something is still using the same path the missing patrol took.
intended: I want to see who or what is on the track before I go any farther from the gate.

text: I shift a few paces along the brush for a clearer angle and ease a wet branch aside, trying to make out the shape that is moving in the cover.
motivation: Something is slipping through the underbrush just out of sight, and I still cannot tell what it is.
intended: I want a clear look at it before I follow any farther or turn back to the gate.

text: I step out of the brush onto the track where the shape can see me and call over, asking whether they came from the gate or from farther up the patrol route.
motivation: A figure is moving carefully near the crates on the missing patrol's path, pausing as if it is listening.
intended: I want them to stop and answer so I can tell who is using this track.

text: I walk toward the still patch of brush at a steady pace, hands empty and in sight, until I can tell whether a person, an animal, or only wet leaves is waiting there.
motivation: The figure froze when I called and gave no answer, so it is still somewhere in that cover.
intended: I want a clear look at it, or to make it move so I can see what it is and which way it goes.

text: I grab the wet branches in front of the outline and pull them wide, so whatever is standing on the track has no cover left.
motivation: I can see an outline in the brush, and it still will not show itself or answer.
intended: I want a plain look at what is on the track, person or otherwise.

text: I stay where I am and look the figure over for a face, clothes, a weapon, or any badge or gear that would tie it to Eldrin Voss's patrol.
motivation: The cover is gone and the shape is crouched in the open, uneasy, but I still cannot tell what it is.
intended: I want one clear detail that says whether this is a person from the patrol or something else.

text: I leave the figure in the brush and follow the muddy track farther northwest, watching the ruts and the verges for anything a patrol might have dropped.
motivation: That shape has no face, badge, weapon, or patrol gear, so it is not the lead I came out here for.
intended: I want a real sign of Eldrin Voss's patrol farther along the track.
